clues: A remote protected island ecosystem offers a rare setting for studying natural processes with little direct human disturbance.
Volcanic activity and glacial change can be observed within the same island group.
The protected property includes surrounding marine waters as well as land.
These Australian subantarctic islands lie in the southern Indian Ocean, well away from the mainland.
Find Australia’s remote volcanic World Heritage island pair south-west of the continent, closer to Antarctica than mainland Australia.
targetLabel: Heard and McDonald Islands — designated property reference point
modernContext: UNESCO’s published representative point for the designated property, not its uniquely correct centre.
explanation: The source describes a largely undisturbed subantarctic setting in which volcanic and glacial processes can be studied together. This is not a claim that environmental conditions or introduced-species status can never change. The target is the property’s published representative point, not a landing site or a single volcano.
dateLabel: First UNESCO World Heritage inscription year, not the age of the natural feature
cultures: Physical geography, conservation and scientific study
uncertainty: Source-checked authoring only; independent factual, English and clue-order review is pending. The point represents the designated property, not every part of a large natural feature. Source descriptions and dynamic environmental conditions may differ in date or extent; precise current measurements are not implied.
